Bertrand, Duflo, Mullainathan (2004)

Jim Flynn

October 7, 2026

How Much Should We Trust DiD Estimates?

  • DiD had become common way to evaluate policy
  • Most focused exoegeneity of policy adoption
    • Why is this important?
  • This paper focuses on the standard errors of DiD estimates
    • What are the implications of bad standard errors?

Are standard errors on DiD estimates too small?

  • Authors point to three specific issues with DiD papers
  • Each understates amount of variation that exists
  • They argue serial correlation is especially bad in DiD
    • DiD typically uses long time series (median 16.5)
    • DVs usually highly positively serially correlated
    • Treatment variable changes very little over time

Table I - Assessing the potential problem

Issue

  • It is almost impossible to tell whether serial correlation is a problem for any one paper
    • Maybe it exists but we can’t tell if it drives the result
    • So what do they do?

Placebo estimates

  • Using CPS data on women’s wages from 1979-1999
  • Look at earnings employment status, education
  • Randomly create fake laws and treatment years
  • Treat year randomly drawn from 1985-1995
  • 25 states randomly assigned to be treated
  • Run DiD repeatedly to estimate the effect of ‘laws’
    • Why do this?
    • What do we expect to happen?

Specification

\[Y_{ist} = A_s + B_t + cX_{ist} + \beta I_{st} + \epsilon_{ist}\]

  • \(Y\) is outcome
  • \(A_s\) is state FE
  • \(B_t\) is year FE
  • \(X_{ist}\) are individual controls
  • \(I_{st}\) is treatment indicator

Ok so we have a problem

  • 60 percent of ‘significant’ estimates are in the 1-2% range
  • If you ever read applied papers, this should freak you out
    • What can we do?

Table III Varying N and T

Table IV - Parametric solutions

Block bootstrap

  • We want to get a picture of the sampling variance
  • Bootstrapping does this in general
    • What is bootstrapping?
    • Sampling with replacement from original data
    • Here we are doing this with blocks (states)

Table V

Work great….with lots of states.

Ignoring time series information

  • Big part of the problem is having many periods
  • Can aggregate data into a pre and post period
  • Only works when all laws passed simultaneously
    • Residual aggregation solution

Takeaways

  • The standard DiD estimate can have serious issues
  • Need to be thoughtful about standard errors
    • And potential issues
  • We will see after the midterm that a lot has changed and a lot has stayed the same
